text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.8% today after hitting a two-week high yesterday, likely pulled back by news that the U.S. has struck a deal to import Russian diesel to help ease fuel prices. The agreement undermines the near-term profit potential for American refiners like Marathon, who have been benefiting from tight fuel supplies and elevated prices caused by war-related disruptions and refinery damage. Even though crude prices remain elevated—U.S. oil at $96 and world oil at $125 per barrel—and U.S. refineries are running at 92.7% capacity, an influx of cheap Russian diesel compresses the margins refiners earn on fuel production.

The stock's sharp two-week rally (up 15.6%) had priced in a longer period of supply tightness and geopolitical disruption. Today's pullback reflects investors recalibrating as a major supply relief valve has just opened, reducing the scarcity premium that had driven refiner profits higher.
